title: IBM Db2 13 for z/OS CREATE TRIGGER body statement inventory

baseline.notes: Syntax strings are compact test-authoring summaries. Follow the linked IBM statement syntax diagram for every nested subgrammar and statement-specific restriction.

sql-control-statement.name: SQL-control-statement
sql-control-statement.syntax: <assignment | CALL | CASE | compound | FOR | GET DIAGNOSTICS | GOTO | IF | ITERATE | LEAVE | LOOP | REPEAT | RESIGNAL | SIGNAL | WHILE>
sql-control-statement.summary: One SQL PL control statement. RETURN is listed in the SQL PL overview but is explicitly prohibited in a trigger.

allocate-cursor.name: ALLOCATE CURSOR
allocate-cursor.summary: Allocates a cursor for a result set locator returned by a procedure.

alter-function.name: ALTER FUNCTION
alter-function.summary: Only the function forms listed by IBM's SQL-procedure-statement matrix are admitted; use the matching ALTER FUNCTION syntax diagram.

associate-locators.name: ASSOCIATE LOCATORS
associate-locators.syntax: ASSOCIATE RESULT SET LOCATORS (<locator-variable> [, ...]) WITH PROCEDURE <procedure-name>
associate-locators.summary: Captures result set locator values returned by an earlier CALL.

call.name: CALL
call.summary: Invokes a local procedure; transaction-control and BEFORE-trigger restrictions still apply transitively.

close.name: CLOSE
close.summary: Closes a declared or allocated cursor.

comment.name: COMMENT
comment.summary: Adds or removes a catalog comment by using one of the statement's object-specific forms.

create-index.name: CREATE INDEX
create-index.summary: Uses the complete CREATE INDEX grammar already modeled by this KB.

create-table.name: CREATE TABLE
create-table.summary: Uses the complete CREATE TABLE grammar already modeled by this KB, but a trigger-body CREATE TABLE cannot include LOB or XML columns.

create-view.name: CREATE VIEW
create-view.syntax: CREATE VIEW <view-name> [(<column-name> [, ...])] AS [WITH <common-table-expression> [, ...]] <fullselect> [WITH [CASCADED | LOCAL] CHECK OPTION]
create-view.summary: Creates a view using the statement-specific fullselect and check-option rules; an omitted check-option qualifier defaults to CASCADED.

declare-cursor.name: DECLARE CURSOR
declare-cursor.summary: Declares a static or prepared-statement cursor in a compound block.

delete-searched.name: DELETE (searched)
delete-searched.summary: Deletes qualifying target rows; positioned DELETE is a different syntax path.

drop.name: DROP
drop.summary: The trigger subset permits only DROP TABLE, DROP VIEW, and DROP INDEX.

execute.name: EXECUTE
execute.summary: Executes a statement prepared under a declared statement name.

execute-immediate.name: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
execute-immediate.summary: Prepares and executes one dynamically constructed SQL statement.

explain.name: EXPLAIN
explain.summary: Uses one of the documented EXPLAIN forms; required explain tables and privileges remain prerequisites.

fetch.name: FETCH
fetch.summary: In SQL PL trigger bodies, FETCH cannot specify orientation, multiple-row fetch, WITH CONTINUE, or CURRENT CONTINUE.

fullselect.name: fullselect
fullselect.summary: A stand-alone query supported only by basic triggers; a BEFORE-trigger fullselect cannot reference the subject table.

get-diagnostics.name: GET DIAGNOSTICS
get-diagnostics.summary: Retrieves diagnostics for the previous statement; error diagnostics must be fetched as the first executable handler statement.

grant.name: GRANT
grant.summary: Uses the applicable object-specific GRANT form. IBM's trigger matrix links notes 4 and 7; note 7's text is CREATE TABLE-specific, so no extra GRANT rule is inferred from it.

insert.name: INSERT
insert.summary: Inserts one or more rows using the statement-specific atomicity and include-column forms.

label.name: LABEL
label.summary: Sets the label for an eligible Db2 object by using the matching object form.

lock-table.name: LOCK TABLE
lock-table.summary: Acquires an explicit table or eligible partition lock.

merge.name: MERGE
merge.syntax: MERGE INTO <target> [AS <correlation>] USING <source> ON <search-condition> <WHEN MATCHED|NOT MATCHED clauses>
merge.summary: Applies conditional update, delete, or insert operations using the full MERGE grammar.

open.name: OPEN
open.summary: Opens a declared cursor, optionally supplying values for parameter markers in a prepared select.

prepare.name: PREPARE
prepare.summary: Prepares a dynamic statement for EXECUTE or for a cursor declared against the statement name.

refresh-table.name: REFRESH TABLE
refresh-table.summary: Refreshes an eligible materialized query table.

rename.name: RENAME
rename.summary: Renames an eligible table or index; a table with a trigger defined on it cannot itself be renamed.

revoke.name: REVOKE
revoke.summary: Uses the applicable object-specific REVOKE form.

savepoint.name: SAVEPOINT
savepoint.syntax: SAVEPOINT <savepoint-name> [UNIQUE] ON ROLLBACK RETAIN CURSORS [ON ROLLBACK RETAIN LOCKS]
savepoint.summary: Sets a savepoint; direct use is excluded from BEFORE triggers and procedures containing it cannot be called by a trigger.

select-into.name: SELECT INTO
select-into.summary: Retrieves a single result row into SQL or transition-compatible targets.

set-assignment.name: SET assignment-statement
set-assignment.summary: Assigns transition variables, SQL variables, array elements, or supported global variables according to context; a basic trigger target must be a transition variable.

set-special-register.name: SET special-register
set-special-register.summary: Allowed in an advanced trigger except SET CURRENT PACKAGE PATH and SET CURRENT PACKAGESET.

signal.name: SIGNAL
signal.summary: Raises an application condition; the legacy parenthesized diagnostic expression is trigger-only compatibility syntax.

truncate.name: TRUNCATE
truncate.syntax: TRUNCATE TABLE <table-name> [DROP STORAGE | REUSE STORAGE] [IGNORE DELETE TRIGGERS | RESTRICT WHEN DELETE TRIGGERS] IMMEDIATE
truncate.summary: Deletes all rows using the statement's storage and delete-trigger choices.

update-searched.name: UPDATE (searched)
update-searched.summary: Updates qualifying target rows; positioned UPDATE is a different syntax path.

values.name: VALUES
values.summary: A stand-alone VALUES statement supported only by basic triggers.

values-into.name: VALUES INTO
values-into.summary: Assigns one row of expression results to targets.

notes: The BEGIN ATOMIC list can contain only the same closed triggered-SQL-statement set.
The statements execute in source order.
Basic SET assignment targets must be transition variables.
Stand-alone fullselect and VALUES are basic-only body forms.

restrictions: Target must be a transition variable.

notes: The body is one outer statement. Use a compound SQL-control-statement for multiple statements.
Nested statements in a control statement are limited to the trigger-supported rows of SQL-procedure-statement.
Stand-alone fullselect and VALUES are not advanced triggered-SQL-statements; use SELECT INTO and VALUES INTO.
Activation-time restrictions apply recursively to statements nested in control statements.

restrictions: The created table must not include LOB or XML columns.
Nested content inherits every statement-specific and BEFORE-trigger restriction.
Must be nested in an SQL-control-statement; it is not an advanced direct triggered-SQL-statement.
Must not include LOB or XML columns.
Must be nested in an SQL-control-statement; it is not an advanced direct triggered-SQL-statement.
Must be nested in an SQL-control-statement; it is not an advanced direct triggered-SQL-statement.
Only DROP TABLE, DROP VIEW, and DROP INDEX are allowed.
No fetch orientation, multiple-row fetch, WITH CONTINUE, or CURRENT CONTINUE.
IBM's table also links its CREATE TABLE LOB/XML note to GRANT; that note text is not treated as a GRANT semantic rule.
SET CURRENT PACKAGE PATH and SET CURRENT PACKAGESET are excluded.

excluded: ALTER PROCEDURE (external, SQL - external, or SQL - native)

restrictions: The outermost advanced-trigger compound statement is ATOMIC by default and cannot specify NOT ATOMIC.

control_statements.syntax: [<label>:] FOR [<loop-name> AS] [<cursor-name> CURSOR [WITH|WITHOUT HOLD] FOR] <select-statement> DO <SQL-procedure-statement>; [...] END FOR [<label>]

restrictions: The RETURN statement must not be specified in a trigger.
